items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Johnny Russell (tenor), both of whom I had worked with in Benny Carter's band in 1933

ctx.x: For some unknown reason, Benny began to lose interest in the band and Bill Dillard left to join Teddy Hill who had been the tenor man with Luis Russell at one time and now had his own band at the Savoy. Two weeks before the time for us to finish at the Empire, Benny told us that he would be disbanding.

The word got around very quickly and Teddy Hill asked me and Dickie Wells to join his band. Willie Bryant was an M.C. and showman who had an act with another showman named Leonard Reed, who was forming an orchestra, and he engaged Teddy Wilson, Johnny Russell, Glyn Pacque and Cozy Cole. We all hated to see this band of Benny's break up and I considered and still do consider it the best band I ever played with.

So in January of 1934, Dickie Wells and I joined Teddy at the Savoy and I was back home again. The other members of the band were Bernard Flood, who along with Dillard and myself were the trumpet section. Hoe Britton was the other trombonist. Howard Johnson and Harold Blanchard on alto saxs and Leon 'Chu' Berry on tenor sax, Sam Allen, piano, John Smith, guitar, Richard 'Dick' Fullbright, bass and Bill Geeson on drums.

items.q: The rest of the musicians were ... Johnny Russel, tenor. ... as the rhythm section.

ctx.x: Benny said that he would let me know when the band would begin rehearsing so I went to Leonia, New Jersey, to spend a couple of days with Beezie whom I had not seen for four months. She was working and could not meet me when I returned to New York. When I came from Leonia I learned from Dickie Wells who was also engaged to play with Benny that the band had made some records for an English arranger named Spike Hughes. No one knew where to contact me in New Jersey so I missed my first chance to record with Benny…

But I made the other rehearsals. Benny had discovered three musicians who were in New York. The pianist, Teddy Wilson, Frederic 'Keg' Johnson, a trombonist and George Johnson (no relation to Keg) an alto sax player. The rest of the musicians were Charlie 'Big' Green, ex-Henderson Trombonist, Dickie Wells, trombone, Bill Dillard, Lindon (Lincoln) Mills and myself on trumpets, Glyn Paque, alto sax and Johnny Russel, tenor.
